# Spam updates

*Update* · also written spam update

Updates to Google's spam-detection systems, announced on the Search Status Dashboard.

**Glossary** (*Spam update*): A notable improvement to Google's automated spam detection systems, such as SpamBrain, listed with its ranking updates. Spam updates target spam pages; to recover, a site removes the spam Google described.

Narrative: the topic [Core updates and spam updates](../topics/search-updates.md) tells the story; this card lists what links to it.

18 claims mention it: 6 from Google's documentation, 10 shown or said at the event (1 confirmed by Google docs, 8 consistent with Google docs, 1 nothing to verify), 2 the author's analysis. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [Google Search spam updates and your site](https://developers.google.com/search/updates/spam-updates), [Google Search Status Dashboard](https://status.search.google.com/incidents/XhUDXP7A67iHCD2kmbVu).

- [`D2-C978`](../sessions/D2-S16-lightning-session-g-internationalisation.md) Docs: Google's October 2023 spam update post (4 October 2023) says the update improved coverage in many languages and spam types, cleaning up spam reported in Turkish, Vietnamese, Indonesian, Hindi, Chinese and other languages, particularly cloaking, hacked, auto-generated and scraped spam. `[D2-C978, docs, Search Central blog (4 October 2023), https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2023/10/october-2023-spam-update]`
- [`D3-C202`](../sessions/D3-S05-how-google-thinks-about-quality.md) Docs: Google's Search Status Dashboard says the September 2026 spam update began on 24 September 2026, applies globally to all languages and may take up to two weeks to roll out. `[D3-C202, docs, Google Search Status Dashboard (Ranking incident history), Google Search Status Dashboard (September 2026 spam update), https://status.search.google.com/products/rGHU1u87FJnkP6W2GwMi/history]`
- [`D3-C261`](../sessions/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) Docs: As of 3 October 2026, the Ranking history of Google's Search Status Dashboard lists two core updates in 2026 (March and May) and four spam updates (March, June, August and September). `[D3-C261, docs, Google Search Status Dashboard (Ranking incident history), https://status.search.google.com/products/rGHU1u87FJnkP6W2GwMi/history]`
- [`D3-C287`](../sessions/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) Docs: Google's spam updates page says its automated spam detection systems run constantly, and a notable improvement to them, such as to the AI-based SpamBrain system, is called a spam update and listed with Google's ranking updates. `[D3-C287, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/updates/spam-updates]`
- [`D3-C291`](../sessions/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) Docs: Google's spam updates page says that after a spam update, changes may help a site improve if Google's automated systems learn over a period of months that the site complies with its spam policies. `[D3-C291, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/updates/spam-updates]`
- [`D3-C292`](../sessions/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) Docs: Google's spam updates page says that after a link spam update, fixing the site might not bring an improvement, because any ranking benefit the spammy links had generated is lost and cannot be regained. `[D3-C292, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/updates/spam-updates]`

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D3-C201`](../sessions/D3-S05-how-google-thinks-about-quality.md) Stage, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: Google's quality talk said Google had released four spam updates in 2026 by the time of the talk on 2 October, with one still rolling out. `[D3-C201, stage, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C203`](../sessions/D3-S05-how-google-thinks-about-quality.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Google's quality talk said its spam updates mostly target spam pages, so most site owners in the audience were probably not affected. `[D3-C203, stage, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C205`](../sessions/D3-S05-how-google-thinks-about-quality.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Google's quality talk said AI has fundamentally changed how Google builds spam updates, letting it evaluate many more candidates and drastically increasing its velocity, so it launches faster with more impact. `[D3-C205, stage, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C250`](../sessions/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Every kind of Search update, whether a feature launch, a core update or a spam update, has the same goal: satisfying users' information needs with better results. `[D3-C250, stage, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C286`](../sessions/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: When spammers find loopholes that Google's systems miss, Google releases spam updates that change its systems to catch them. `[D3-C286, stage, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C288`](../sessions/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Spam updates target only spam: they go after sites that churn out millions of low-quality pages to make money, very likely not the site owners and SEOs in the audience. `[D3-C288, stage, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C289`](../sessions/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) Slide, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Google's 'Recoveries' slide said that to recover from a spam update a site should remove the kind of spam Google described in its blog announcements of the update. `[D3-C289, slide, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C293`](../sessions/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: A ranking drop after a core update is not a penalty, so technically there is no recovery from a core update in the way there is after a spam update. `[D3-C293, stage, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C663`](../sessions/D3-S17-how-long-does-it-take-to.md) Slide, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Google estimated that a spam update affects sites within 1-2 days of the rollout, 1-2 weeks for continuous processing (said on stage as 2 weeks on average) and months for batch refreshes. `[D3-C663, slide, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C290`](../sessions/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) Stage, Day 3, nothing to verify: The speaker declined to give a timeline for recovering from a spam update, saying the update had targeted spam. `[D3-C290, stage, Google, Day 3]`

## The author's analysis

- [`D2-C979`](../sessions/D2-S16-lightning-session-g-internationalisation.md) Analysis: The October 2023 spam update cited in the non-Latin-script talk names neither Persian nor Arabic (only 'other languages') and lists cloaking, hacked, auto-generated and scraped spam, not link spam, so it does not show that the bought links the presenter saw working in Persian or Arabic search were addressed. `[D2-C979, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D3-C157`](../sessions/D3-S05-how-google-thinks-about-quality.md) Analysis: Google made 4,781 launches to Search in 2023 while its status dashboard lists nine named ranking updates that year, so almost every change to Search goes unannounced; monitor rankings and traffic continuously, not only around announced core or spam updates. `[D3-C157, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
